directive.quote: New home: a new tool in this repo (trillion-workshop) at tools/<plain-job-name>/. Reuse the SSH helper (administrationArguments) instead of copying it.

old_copy.deleted_with: the Trillion-X/trillion pull request that deletes scripts/portable-receptionist-build.mjs, its test and its callers, merged after this one

preserve: git archive of one verified commit is the only source that travels: no home folder, Git configuration, uncommitted file, credential or account database
the revision is checked by the same pattern and resolved to a full 40-character commit before anything reaches the host
the build is --locked and --release for the trillion-mcp-receptionist binary, then its bootstrap_consumes_and_closes_the_original_credential_descriptor test runs
the build unpacks under umask 077 into a folder named by the commit, and a failed build answers the last 120 lines of its log
the built file is refused unless it is the file built from that commit, then checked and made 0755
ssh reaches the host only through the administration arguments: one key file, the pinned host key, batch mode
allowed_deltas: every host path (source_root, cargo_home, rustup_home, swap path, install_path), port, user and the Rust toolchain version is a declared input instead of /opt/trillion/source, /root/.cargo and root

the build-machine lines of scripts/portable-service-host-setup.sh (2-4 and 26-35: packages, folders, swap, rustup) are the prepare operation, with the packages, swap and toolchain from the request; its service-user and sshd lines stay with the door tunnel
inspect reads the request's ports and service user instead of 18789, 9443, 443 and trillion-identity
the optional build cache outside the commit folder is dropped: the old check allowed only the commit folder's own target, so it was never used
install can also put a copy at install_path in one rename
the command line takes the Workshop request on stdin and the held key file in argv, prints { result } or { error }, and keeps no readback file between runs; dry_run answers what would run
the administration arguments come from tools/administer-a-rented-host, packed by the rows
banned_substitutions: a host, path, port, user or toolchain written into the code
sending a working tree instead of git archive of a commit
reading the administration key in this program

tools/build-and-install-the-public-receptionist/test/receptionist-build.test.mjs build (run): archives one committed tree with real git, sends it and builds that commit
tools/build-and-install-the-public-receptionist/test/receptionist-build.test.mjs install (run): checks the built file, makes it runnable and puts a copy at install_path in one rename
